newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver stable post-shakedown-for now.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver stable post-shakedown-for now.

text.p: Gold and silver prices were static on Monday after tumbling to fresh lows last week, but the market was apprehensive about a fresh downside assault.
"I think everyone's looking for the bottom in this market but no one has the courage to call it," a dealer said.
Gold closed just $0.50 lower at $381.25 an ounce in London, while silver ended one cent firmer compared to Friday at $4.88.
Palladium, however, crumbled under pressure from weakness in fellow industrial metal silver, and fixed at a new three-year low before closing at $117.75, down $2.00 from Friday.
Silver plummeted below its key $5.00 an ounce level last Thursday and slid further on Friday in a speculative play by U.S. investment funds.
Gold was bruised in the process, shedding about $2.00 and trading at 2-1/2 month lows, but has hung on above the important $380 support level so far.
Dealers said another push could be forthcoming from big funds intent on further depressing gold prices.
"I think the funds tried silver on Thursday and Friday to get gold lower, and they want a bigger break down on gold. There may be another attack on the downside," a dealer said.

Gold was finding decent support for now around $380, but that may not last, analysts said. "If we're going to see a major move in gold at all, then it will be down," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Silver's downside targets were more nebulous, although some analysts have named $4.75 and $4.60.
"Pick a number," a dealer said. A test of the $4.80-$4.82 an ounce support level was seen likely in the next few days.
Silver's weakness was heaping pressure on the other white metals, with platinum fixing at a fresh low for nearly 2-1/2 years at $386.50 an ounce. It closed at the same level.
But platinum was still holding up above key support at $385 so far, dealers said.
They were less optimistic about palladium, pegging its targets at $115 and then $112.
"It's been panicky long liquidation. The selling in silver just pushed over a few more of the specs who decided there's not much hope for the precious metals," a dealer said.
Palladium and platinum markets have been undermined by ample supplies from Russia into slack demand over the summer and will likely require some time to absorb the excess metal, he said.
